answer.rationale: Hard expiry in 14 days with the line at 94% and no buffer makes delivery risk the binding constraint. Deferral is not analogous to c5 (this contract does not continue month-to-month). Switching primary to take the 18% quote would meet finance’s number but would add onboarding/integration risk on a no-buffer line, which violates the stated objective; c2 is therefore treated as unverified competitive context, not as license to cut over. Adding a second source (c3) does not replace the expiring primary in this cycle. One decision is therefore a c4/c6-style renegotiation of the incumbent—using the low-cost quote and possible term/volume as leverage—to pursue the spend cut without a supplier migration (c1). Uncertain whether the incumbent can actually deliver ~18%; that is why c2’s archive should be checked and why this is not a broad vendor rollout.
